chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abī Naṣr al-Bazanṭī narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: “Our companions narrate that shaving the head outside of hajj or ‘umrah is mutilation.”
So he said: “Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, when he completed his rites, would go to a village called Sāyah and shave his head there.”

key_terms.الرَّأْسِ: the head, the part being shaved
key_terms.حَلْقَ: shaving, specifically the shaving of the head
key_terms.سَايَةُ: Sāyah, the name of the village mentioned

ai.seo_question: Is shaving the head outside of hajj or ‘umrah considered mutilation in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the issue of shaving the head outside the immediate context of hajj and ‘umrah. The Imam عليه السلام answers by citing the practice of Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام after completing his rites, indicating a precedent relevant to this juristic question.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3124 - Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti narrated from Abu Al-Hasan (as):
I said to him, "Our companions narrate that shaving the head outside of Hajj or Umrah is considered mutilation."
Imam (as) replied: "Abu Al-Hasan (as), after completing his rituals, would go to a village called Sāyah and shave his head there."
